**The meaning of the verses**
﴿وَأَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ وَلَا تَنَازَعُوا فَتَفْشَلُوا وَتَذْهَبَ رِيحُكُمْ ۖ وَاصْبِرُوا ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الصَّابِرِينَ﴾
Hold to obeying Allah and obeying His Messenger in all your circumstances, and do not disagree so that your word is divided and your hearts differ, and you become weak and your strength and victory go away. And be patient when you meet the enemy. Allah is with the patient, with His help, victory and support, and He will never abandon them.

﴿وَاعْتَصِمُوا بِحَبْلِ اللَّهِ جَمِيعًا وَلَا تَفَرَّقُوا﴾
And hold on, all of you, to the Book of your Lord and the guidance of your Prophet, and do not do anything that leads to your division.

📖 At-Tafsir Al-Muyassar — King Fahd Complex.

**Talk with your child**
1. What did Hamdan say in the boat? And did he mean anything by it? And why did his words stay in his two friends' hearts?
2. Why did their boat stand still while the other boats sailed in the very same wind? And how did it start moving again?
3. Is every difference of opinion a blameworthy quarrel? (No; for each person to have their opinion and for them to consult calmly is good. What is blameworthy is when the disagreement turns into quarrelling, where each one counts his own work and forgets his friend's, so hearts are divided and hands grow weak.)

**This week's exercise**
Choose a job at home that the brothers and sisters do together (tidying a room or laying the table), and they agree on who does what. At the end, each one mentions something good that their brother or sister did, not what they did themselves.
